summary: Host/credential coherence guard is fully implemented. The PUT /api/repositories/:id/credential handler in src/server/routes/repositories.ts already contains the guard (lines 286–298): it calls extractHost(repo.Url), compares against credential.host, and returns HTTP 400 with a descriptive error message when they differ. The guard is skipped for null credentialId (clear) and SSH URLs (extractHost returns null). Three specific coherence test cases are present in repositories.test.ts: mismatched host → 400 with both hosts in error message, matching host → 200, and null (clear) → 200. Both docs/agents/project-manifest/rest-api.md and docs/agents/project-manifest/constraints.md already document the guard. All 30 repository route tests pass.

summary: Reviewed 4 files (repositories.ts, repositories.test.ts, rest-api.md, constraints.md) plus supporting modules (git-credentials.ts, repository-orchestrator.ts, workspace-orchestrator.ts). 0 Critical, 0 High findings. 1 Medium (information disclosure — echoes user-supplied credentialId and internal credential.host in error response body; acceptable for a local-only admin tool with no auth layer). 1 Info (orchestrators do not re-validate host coherence at use time; by design — the API-layer guard closes the gap at assignment, so stored CredentialIds are always coherent). Security sign-off: PASS.

comments.note: Medium — A05/Information Exposure | repositories.ts line 294 | The 400 error message echoes the caller-supplied credentialId and the internal credential.host value: 'Credential "${credentialId}" is configured for host "${credential.host}" but repository URL resolves to "${repoHost}".' Both values are user-controlled or admin-visible in this local tool, so practical impact is negligible. In a multi-tenant web context this pattern could constitute internal config disclosure. Remediation (if scope ever expands): return a generic message like 'Credential host does not match repository host' and log detail server-side.

Info — A04/Design | git-credentials.ts resolveCredential() / orchestrators | resolveCredential() with explicit credentialId does not cross-validate host coherence at use time (documented in @remarks). The WP-008 guard in PUT /api/repositories/:id/credential closes this gap at assignment time, making all persisted CredentialId values coherent. No additional runtime re-validation is required. Design is sound.

No Critical or High security findings. All OWASP Top 10 categories reviewed: A01 (no IDOR; guard enforces host constraint), A02 (tokens masked in credential-options response; URL encoding via WHATWG API), A03 (no injection — credentialId compared by strict equality; extractHost uses WHATWG URL parser; injectCredentialToken uses URL.username assignment), A04 (SSH exemption and null-clear path are intentional and correctly implemented), A05 (500 paths return generic messages), A06 (no new dependencies), A07 (local-only tool, no auth layer by design), A08 (type-guarded body parsing; no unsafe deserialization), A09 (audit log entries for assign-credential and clear-credential emitted correctly), A10 (no SSRF — no server-side URL fetch triggered by the credential endpoint).
